audit.whatIsWrong: The first three level-chart rows contradict their own why text. whys[0] ends 'you control the first exchanges' but win[0] is Skill; whys[1] calls level 2 'your cleanest spike of the lane' but win[1] is Rumble; whys[2] opens 'it stays even' but win[2] is Rumble.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble] and matches every why line.
audit.corrected: Three rows flipped as one atomic group in both layers; the two Gnar rows rated 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phases were untouched template text, and the page's designated cooldown to track is Scrap Shield — which is 6 seconds flat. There is no such thing as playing around a 6-second shield; the numbers that decide this lane are his Heat bar and your own Wallop at a flat 7s.
audit.why: Kit file: Scrap Shield 6s, Flamespitter 10s falling to 6s, Electro Harpoon 0.5s between two charges, The Equalizer 130s at rank 1. The mirror audit established Wallop as the flat 7s stun and GNAR! as the 90-to-30s one-off.
audit.corrected: All seven phases rewritten with the Heat threshold, Wallop's 7s and Flamespitter's 600-range cone; dosFull[2].d now says outright that a 6s shield is bled, not baited.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says he harpoon-slows you onto an Equalizer line 'so you can't Hop out of the burn'. A slow does not stop a dash — the mirror audit already established that The Equalizer burns and slows but does not wall off Hop, and Hop goes over it.
audit.why: Riot's R text is a wall of flames that damages and slows; nothing in it denies mobility. The two directions of this matchup must not disagree, and the mirror page now states the Hop-goes-over rule explicitly.
audit.corrected: Rewritten so the harpoon slow costs you burn ticks before the Hop lands, rather than denying the Hop. dontsFull[1].d states the same rule from your side.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr, winCon and dosFull[1] all say 'Build MR', and dosFull[1].d was a copy-paste of the trading line. Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist on hit and he carries two charges, so flat MR is partly shredded before the damage lands.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'electrocuting his target with magic damage, slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist.' That is the reason health and Heat management matter alongside MR here.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten to name the items and the MR shred.

edits.after: Electro Harpoon-slow you onto an Equalizer line so the burn ticks before your Hop lands

edits.after: Rumble has zero heat and must walk into melee range at 1, while Mini Gnar pokes with autos and a Boomerang slow.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Rumble's Scrap Shield is down.
edits.after: Your level-2 Hyper third-hit plus a Boomerang slow is a free chunk and shove while his heat bar is empty.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Rumble must walk into your range.
edits.after: Even kiting his immobile body, but a near-overheat Flamespitter out-DPSes you inside the 600-range cone.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Scrap Shield's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 hinge on Rage: a 7s Wallop stuns him through Scrap Shield, but stuck in Mini you burn inside Flamespitter.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Rumble's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Equalizer carpets a fire line and you gain no new spell at 6, but Hop or Crunch takes you straight out of the zone.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Scrap Shield's cooldown.
edits.after: His first AP item overheats Flamespitter and out-DPSes your form-locked burst windows.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Rumble carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Sustained burn and Equalizer melt your Mega bulk while Scrap Shield blunts the all-in — he owns the side lane.

edits.before: Boomerang Rumble's last-hits, AA-hop out of his reach, and time Mega so the transform lands ON his engage window.
edits.after: Mercury's Treads and a Spectre's Cowl, but Electro Harpoon shreds MR, so health matters as much as resistance.

edits.before: Rumble wastes Scrap Shield — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Scrap Shield is only 6s — poke to bleed heat, not to break it.

edits.before: That is Rumble's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Above 50% Heat his Danger Zone gives every basic ability a bonus effect.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The Equalizer burns and slows; your Hop still goes over it.

notes: IMPORTANT DATA DEFECT: the kit file tags Scrap Shield (W) with knockup and terrain flags, and the _missing file therefore raises a 'knockup-enabler: GNAR! (R) vs Scrap Shield (W)' interaction for this matchup. Riot's W text is a shield plus a burst of speed and nothing else — Rumble has no displacement in his kit. I did NOT write that interaction anywhere; it is a tooltip-parse misfire and any agent who takes that _missing headline at face value will invent a knockup Rumble does not have. packet.defects also flags 'Electro Harpoon-slow' in wants.foe[2] as a wrong name — false positive, the hyphenated compound is the edit distance. Separately, focus.text and the whole cooldown-tracking frame of this page point at Scrap Shield, a 6-second ability; the matchup-defining cooldown is really his Heat bar and The Equalizer at 130s, which is a page-level restructure rather than a field edit.
